commit.message:
feat(testing): ship enforce_rls as a pytest plugin, add assert_rls_enforced() (#97) (#140)

* feat(testing): ship enforce_rls as a pytest plugin, add assert_rls_enforced() (#97)

A superuser or BYPASSRLS connection skips every RLS policy, so isolation
tests on it pass whether or not the policies work. The role-switching
fixtures from tests/conftest.py now ship as a pytest plugin.

- django_rls_tenants/pytest_plugin.py, registered through the pytest11
  entry point "django_rls_tenants" (-p no:django_rls_tenants opts out).
  It sits at the package root, not in tenants/, because pytest imports it
  before Django settings exist and tenants/__init__.py imports models; it
  imports nothing from Django at module level.
- Fixtures: rls_role (session; creates the role NOLOGIN if missing, grants
  USAGE on the search_path schemas, ALL on their tables and sequences and
  default privileges for later ones; rejects an existing BYPASSRLS role;
  tolerates a concurrent CREATE ROLE from an xdist worker), enforce_rls
  (SET ROLE / RESET ROLE on each configured alias that bypasses RLS,
  skipping aliases the test may not use) and enforce_rls_on_other_threads.
- ini options rls_role (default rls_test_role, validated identifier) and
  rls_role_aliases (default "default").
- assert_rls_enforced() / aassert_rls_enforced() in tenants/testing.py.
- The library suite dogfoods the plugin (replica and pooled stay in
  conftest, built on rls_role); the example suite gets an autouse
  enforce_rls and an assert_rls_enforced() test, so it also passes as the
  Docker superuser.
- CI wheel check requires pytest_plugin.py and the entry point; pytest
  joins the dev group for mypy.
- Docs: testing guide section (fixtures, grants, ini options, limitations,
  TestCase recipe), API reference, W005 troubleshooting, installation,
  CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md, contributing guides, example README.

* fix(pytest_plugin): review fixes for the enforce_rls plugin (#97)

- enforce_rls switches a connection the test closes and reopens again as it
  opens (a connection_created receiver for the test thread, sharing the
  factory with enforce_rls_on_other_threads), and the teardown skips a
  closed connection instead of reopening it to RESET ROLE.
- rls_role fails with a clear message when first requested inside a test
  transaction (request.getfixturevalue() in a non-transactional test): the
  rollback would drop the role and every later enforce_rls test would fail
  with "role does not exist".
- Testing guide: the RLSTestCase example checks whether the connection
  bypasses RLS before CREATE ROLE / GRANT, so it works on a plain role too;
  limitations updated.

commit.message:
feat(affinity): keep every connection's RLS GUCs in step with the active context (#41) (#136)

* feat(affinity): keep every connection's RLS GUCs in step with the active context (#41)

Add the GUC affinity guard (tenants/affinity.py), an execute wrapper that the
connection_created handler installs first on every PostgreSQL connection.
Before each statement on an alias in RLS_TENANTS["DATABASES"] it compares the
admin and tenant GUC values of the active context with what the library last
left on that session, and applies the context's values in one set_config()
statement when they differ.

- thread_sensitive=False hops, asyncio.to_thread() and the error pages Django
  builds on a worker thread under ASGI run with the request's context; the
  worker connection loses it before its first statement without one. The #130
  tests now expect the authenticated page to see its own tenant.
- Sibling asyncio tasks of one request each run with their own context.
- Every configured alias follows a context, whichever alias it was entered on.
- The context comes from a private ContextVar (state._context_gucs) that only
  the library's entry points set; the public state functions never drive it.
- The library's own GUC writes run in writing() and are recorded. The tracker
  follows the libpq transaction status, savepoints, ROLLBACK/COMMIT and
  RESET/DISCARD ALL, and re-applies whatever it cannot tell. Transaction
  control statements, failed transactions and needs_rollback are never
  reconciled. Session GUCs only: inactive with USE_LOCAL_SET=True.
- The middleware cleanup resets the new ContextVar first; the request_finished
  safety net clears it. _apply_request_gucs writes to the signal's connection.

About 1.5 us of Python per statement.

* fix(affinity): review fixes for the GUC affinity guard (#41)

Six independent reviews (correctness, security, tests with mutation testing,
code quality, docs, performance) found tracker lies, an escaped-context
regression and test gaps. Fixed:

- Copies of a context that outlive its block (a task started and not awaited,
  copy_context()) no longer keep its rights: the private ContextVar holds a
  _Live holder that the block's exit ends for every copy.
- Django's commit and rollback of the connection are followed exactly (the
  connection's _commit/_rollback are wrapped), so a transaction boundary the
  guard cannot see no longer leaves a stale record.
- A SQL COMMIT/END of a failed transaction is followed as the rollback it is.
- The statement parser skips leading comments, forgets compound and unreadable
  statements, folds identifiers ASCII-only, handles quoted RESET and tells
  PREPARE TRANSACTION from a prepared statement.
- A swallowed restore failure records unknown values; a block's exit settles
  the thread's other configured aliases; install() keeps the record of a
  session it already tracks.
- RLSTenantMiddleware.__call__ ends the context when a BaseException skips
  process_response (WSGI).
- ContextGucs named tuple and context._rls_state() replace bare tuples and
  three hand-managed tokens per entry point; faster fast path.
- Tests for every finding, shared tests/session_gucs.py, docs corrected
  (using= widening, escaped copies, limits), mkdocs anchor validation.

* fix(affinity): second review round for the GUC affinity guard (#41)

- Django's commit/rollback hooks read the transaction status before and after:
  a commit of a failed transaction (a raw SQL error caught inside atomic()) is
  the rollback PostgreSQL makes it, and a call that ended nothing (psycopg2 in
  autocommit mode) is ignored.
- A block that a copy of a context entered, and that exits after the
  enclosing context has ended, clears the GUCs instead of restoring the ended
  context's values (also on the cancelled-entry path).
- A cancelled sync_to_async call no longer hands its caller a block that
  still runs in another thread: a block's holder compares equal to any value,
  so asgiref's copy-back (!=) leaves the caller's context in place. Only
  process_request's holder is copied back. Context exits end exactly their own
  holder.
- settle_other_aliases() no longer fails or masks a block's exit when another
  alias's connection is broken.
- Savepoint names are parsed exactly; anything after the name makes the values
  unknown.
- Tests for each finding (each re-checked against the reintroduced bug), the
  reviewer's proposed tests for mutation survivors, docs and AGENTS.md updated.

* fix(affinity): review rounds 3 to 7 for the GUC affinity guard (#41)

- Copy rule: a block's holder never replaces a holder the destination
  has (a cancelled sync_to_async call's block), but is copied into one
  without (async_to_sync called inside a block inherits it).
- Every request holds a holder: the one it was served in, its own, or
  one of no context, also after process_exception's hop.
- A block that exits in another Context (a generator closed elsewhere)
  restores its snapshot only on the session it entered on, and no ended
  context's values; the values become unknown.
- A block the view leaves open ends in process_exception, on
  got_request_exception for other 500s, and when the request ends.
- An anonymous request leaves a live context it is served in alone, and
  still clears what its view left behind outside one.
- A non-database exception from a commit leaves the values unknown.
- Docs, CHANGELOG and AGENTS.md updated; documented gaps for 4xx
  responses raised outside the view, exception middleware listed after
  RLSTenantMiddleware and USE_LOCAL_SET=True.

commit.message:
fix(pool): clear RLS GUCs on every checkout from Django's connection pool (#96) (#135)

With Django's psycopg 3 pool (OPTIONS["pool"]), closing a connection
hands it back to psycopg_pool, which only rolls back an open
transaction. Session GUCs set with set_config() survive into the next
checkout. The middleware's cleanup normally clears them, but not when it
failed or reached another connection: a view that closed its connection
before the response ended, a crash, a cancelled request. The
connection_created handler did nothing outside a request context, so the
next borrower (an anonymous request, a Celery task) ran with the
previous request's tenant, admin bypass or extra_bypass_flags. W004
never fired: Django rejects a non-zero CONN_MAX_AGE with a pool.

Django sends connection_created on every checkout. On a pooled alias in
RLS_TENANTS["DATABASES"] the handler now clears every GUC the library's
policies read before the borrower's first query, with or without a
request context, then applies the request's GUCs on the request's
thread as before. "Every GUC the policies read" is the configured tenant
and admin GUCs plus each RLSConstraint's GUCs and extra_bypass_flags and
each RLSM2MConstraint's GUCs, collected from the app registry (cached
once apps.ready, dropped on an INSTALLED_APPS change) and limited to
dotted custom-GUC names, so a name PostgreSQL rejects cannot fail the
statement. The clear is one statement on the connection the signal
sent, committed under AUTOCOMMIT=False. If it fails on a pooled
connection, the connection is closed so the pool discards it and the
error is raised: fail closed. The #130 other-thread clear uses the same
statement, so it now drops bypass flags too.

New django_rls_tenants.pool.reset_rls_gucs is a psycopg_pool reset
callback that runs the same clear when a connection is returned and
leaves it idle; unlike DISCARD ALL / RESET ALL it keeps the time zone
Django sets once per pooled connection. The module is importable from
settings.py before Django is set up. New system check W010 warns for a
pooled alias with USE_LOCAL_SET=False and no reset.

The request_finished safety net now skips a closed connection: with a
pool Django has already returned it, and reopening it checked out
another pooled connection and kept it (for good under ASGI).

Tests: a real psycopg_pool pool of one connection (pooled fixture, role
set through libpq options because Django's assume_role cannot connect
through a pool) covers the anonymous borrower after an early return, two
tenants on one physical connection, a stale bypass flag, a mid-request
re-checkout, a pool with a reset that keeps everything, a failed clear,
USE_LOCAL_SET=True, and reset_rls_gucs (pid-checked, both autocommit
modes, time zone kept). These carry the new psycopg3_only marker, which
conftest deselects on psycopg2 (not skipped). Driver-independent tests
cover the handler branches, the name collection and filter, the
separate-wrapper case, _is_pooled, W010 and the safety net.

Docs: CHANGELOG (Added, Fixed security), connection pooling guide
(Django's Connection Pool, W010), troubleshooting, configuration, API
reference, middleware, security model, migration guide, architecture,
contributing guides, AGENTS.md and the example README.

commit.message:
fix(middleware): keep ASGI error pages from leaving GUCs on worker-thread connections (#130) (#134)

Under ASGI, Django builds some error responses in a
sync_to_async(..., thread_sensitive=False) hop while the request context
is still active: a URL that does not resolve, a view that returns None,
an exception from a process_view or process_template_response hook or
from an async-capable middleware listed after RLSTenantMiddleware. The
hop runs on a default-executor worker thread with its own connection and
a copy of the request's ContextVars. The connection_created handler saw
the copied "GUCs set" flag and set the request's GUCs on the worker's new
connection, and nothing ever cleared them, so a later error page on that
thread, an anonymous visitor's included, ran with the earlier tenant or
with the admin bypass.

The "GUCs set" ContextVar now holds a marker of the thread that set the
GUCs instead of a bool: a _ThreadMarker kept in a threading.local and
compared by identity. threading.get_ident() is not usable, because glibc
hands a finished thread's ident to the next one, and asgiref creates a
thread per request. process_request records the current thread; the
native __acall__ takes the marker from its enter hop, since it runs on
the event-loop thread itself.

connection_created applies the GUCs only on that thread, where the
middleware's cleanup clears them. On any other thread it clears both
GUCs instead, which also drops stale values a reused (pooled) connection
may carry; a failed clear is logged. Database work handed to another
thread with a copy of the context (thread_sensitive=False,
asyncio.to_thread()) therefore runs without the request's context,
under WSGI too. Work that stays on the request's thread is unchanged.

Tests: an AsyncClient regression test with a one-worker default executor
(authenticated, then anonymous, 404 on the same worker thread) over the
native, sync and hook-subclass middleware paths, and the same through a
real ASGIHandler, whose per-request threads also reopen a connection
mid-request; a connection_created receiver runs worker-thread
connections as the RLS test role, so row assertions hold on superuser
legs too. Unit tests cover the handler on another thread, a connection
that arrives with stale GUCs, a second alias, the failed clear, and
which thread owns the GUCs on each middleware path.

Docs: CHANGELOG (Fixed, security), migration guide, middleware guide
(Running under ASGI, multi-database), configuration, security model,
troubleshooting and AGENTS.md.

commit.message:
fix(managers): apply the for_user() context to every method that runs SQL (#131) (#133)

TenantQuerySet.for_user() set the user's GUCs only in _fetch_all(), so
count(), exists(), aggregate(), iterator(), aiterator(), update(),
delete(), create(), bulk_create(), bulk_update(), update_or_create(),
explain() and their async variants ran without them. Under a role that
RLS applies to, and outside a context, they returned zero rows or
counts and inserts were rejected. CI never noticed: every leg connects
as the postgres superuser, which bypasses RLS.

One private context manager, TenantQuerySet._rls_scope(), now wraps the
SQL of each of those methods:

- it resolves the alias once (the router's write alias for writes) and
  pins it on the queryset for the call, so a router that answers
  differently each time cannot split the GUCs from the query;
- it reads both GUCs and sets only those that differ, so inside the
  user's own context (the middleware) it writes nothing;
- it sets the tenant ContextVars, so prefetches, delete() cascades and
  signal handlers are auto-scoped and pass STRICT_MODE;
- on exit it restores the values it found instead of clearing them,
  which keeps an enclosing middleware, tenant_context() or
  admin_context() context intact. Before, a for_user() evaluation
  cleared it (or, with USE_LOCAL_SET, left the for_user() user's values
  set for the rest of the transaction).

iterator() enters the scope once per chunk, never across a yield, so
the loop body does not run as the user and an abandoned loop leaves
nothing behind; aiterator() pulls each chunk in one thread-sensitive
hop. With USE_LOCAL_SET, update_or_create(), bulk_create(),
bulk_update() and delete() open their own transaction when none is
open, as Django runs them in one anyway; other methods raise
RuntimeError outside atomic(), as iteration always did.

Also fixed on the way:

- restore_gucs() skipped the restore while Django had flagged the
  transaction for rollback (a failing pre_delete receiver inside
  delete()), so a caller that caught the error and called
  set_rollback(False) committed the GUCs, admin bypass included;
- STRICT_MODE raised on for_user() + prefetch_related(); cached
  querysets (iteration, count(), exists(), an ordered first()) run no
  query and are no longer checked; aiterator() is now guarded;
- TenantQuerySet.delete() lost Django's queryset_only flag, so
  as_manager() / from_queryset() managers had a table-wide delete().

CI gains a test-plain-role job that runs the library suite as a
non-superuser role (-m "not superuser_only") after verifying the
connection really is one. The test fixtures no longer create a role on
such a connection, enforce_rls also catches BYPASSRLS roles, and the
for_user() tests request enforce_rls so they mean something under the
superuser legs too. Docs: architecture, user integration, protecting
models, STRICT_MODE pages, troubleshooting, roadmap, contributing
guides, the 1.3.4 to 1.4.0 migration guide, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.

commit.message:
fix(testing): assert_rls_blocks_without_context under STRICT_MODE and inside a context (#126) (#132)

The helper's no-context count was an ORM count() run with whatever
state the caller had:

- with STRICT_MODE=True, TenantQuerySet.count() raised
  NoTenantContextError before the query reached PostgreSQL, so suites
  that run with strict mode could not use the helper at all;
- inside rls_bypass() or rls_as_tenant() it counted with that context
  and failed with "RLS may not be enforced", pointing at the wrong
  cause.

Both counts (the admin pre-check and the no-context count) are now raw
SELECT COUNT(*) on the model's quoted db_table, so the strict-mode
guard, the auto-scope filter and default-manager filters are not
involved. The no-context count runs inside rls_context() with the admin
and tenant GUCs cleared on the using connection; they are restored
before the assertion, with SET LOCAL under USE_LOCAL_SET=True, so the
caller's context is intact even when the assertion fails. Bypass flags
are left alone, as documented. The failure message now names the table
and the usual causes. aassert_rls_blocks_without_context() runs the
sync helper in one hop and gets the same fix.

Tests: strict mode (sync and async); inside rls_bypass(),
rls_as_tenant() and their async counterparts, with the caller's GUCs,
ContextVars and raw-SQL visibility checked afterwards; empty table and
table without RLS in both strict modes; a non-default GUC_PREFIX; a
bypass flag left set; a reserved-word table name; restore when the
assertion fails or the count raises; a DatabaseError in the count in
both GUC modes; SET LOCAL restore that does not outlive the commit;
RuntimeError for USE_LOCAL_SET=True outside atomic(); every query on
the using alias (new replica fixture in conftest, sharing the role
switch with enforce_rls). The example project's fail-closed tests no
longer turn STRICT_MODE off.

Docs: testing guide, migration guide (1.3.4 to 1.4.0), CHANGELOG.

commit.message:
feat: supported-versions policy, matrix refresh and drift test (#114) (#124)

* feat: supported-versions policy, matrix refresh and drift test (#114)

Write the supported-versions policy down (installation guide, "Supported
versions"): every Django series upstream still supports; the Python
versions all of them support (intersection); an explicit list of
PostgreSQL majors with CI on the oldest and newest. Dropping an EOL series
is not a breaking change; 1.3.x stays available for Django 4.2-5.1 and
Python 3.11.

Apply it: drop Django 4.2/5.0/5.1 and Python 3.11, add Django 6.1, list
PostgreSQL 15-18 explicitly. requires-python >=3.12, django>=5.2, ruff
py312, mypy 3.12. Relock with --upgrade-package django/django-stubs/mypy
(Django 6.1.2, django-stubs 6.1.2, mypy 2.4.0; tomli gone).

CI: test matrix {3.12, 3.13, 3.14} x {5.2, 6.0, 6.1} with no exclude
rows, a driver axis plus one psycopg 3 include leg on 3.12/6.1 (installed
on top of the synced venv; the verify step asserts the active driver on
every leg), coverage comment/upload moved to 3.12/6.1/psycopg2 (it was
pinned to the dropped 5.1), test-postgres edges {15, 18} x {5.2, 6.1}.

Library: on Django 6.1 the select_related()-without-arguments
RemovedInDjango2028Warning blamed TenantQuerySet.select_related. Emit it
through warn_about_external_use() with this package skipped, so it names
the caller, and set the flag on _chain() the way Django does (keeping
Django's combined-query and values() guards), so Django-internal callers
like the admin changelist are not double-warned. No change on 5.2/6.0.
Correct the select_related(False) comment: Django never accepted False.
Middleware uses self.async_mode (Django >= 5.2); with_rls_context and
_reset_or_clear use PEP 695 type parameters (ruff UP047).

Tests: tests/test_support_matrix.py parses pyproject.toml, ci.yml,
README, docs index, installation guide, comparison page, AGENTS.md, both
contributing guides and example/Dockerfile against one set of constants
(excluded from the sdist; pyyaml added to the test group). A
pytest_configure hook turns every Django RemovedIn*Warning into an error.
Split the select_related() no-args test into caller-attribution,
Django-internal-caller and guard tests; drop the dead Django < 5.0 branch
in test_admin; update the ParamSpec annotation test for PEP 695.

Docs: README/docs index badge and tables, installation guide policy,
AGENTS.md, both contributing guides, comparison page, roadmap Tier 0,
troubleshooting entry for the 6.1 warning, example Dockerfile on Django
6.1, bug template placeholder, CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Verified: ruff, ruff format, mypy, mkdocs --strict, uv lock --check;
866 passed at 93.92% coverage on Django 6.1.2 / Python 3.14 / psycopg2;
866 passed with RLS_FAIL_ON_SKIPPED=1 on Django 5.2.18 and 6.0.9
(Python 3.12), on psycopg 3.3.6 (Django 6.1.2), and on PostgreSQL 18.6
for both test-postgres edges; example makemigrations --check, check and
suite (non-superuser role) on Django 6.1.2; sdist has no
test_support_matrix.py.

* fix(middleware): import MiddlewareMixin from django.middleware when available (#114)

Django main (6.2) moves MiddlewareMixin to django.middleware and turns the
old django.utils.deprecation import into a RemovedInDjango2029Warning via a
module __getattr__. With the test suite treating Django deprecations as
errors, the canary against Django main failed at collection on our own
import (6 collection errors, reproduced locally).

RLSTenantMiddleware now tries django.middleware first and falls back to
django.utils.deprecation on Django 5.2-6.1. The TYPE_CHECKING branch keeps
importing from django.utils.deprecation, where django-stubs 6.1.2 still
declares the class, so mypy keeps the real MiddlewareMixin type instead of
Any. The test helper middleware in tests/rls_views.py does the same.

Verified: ruff, ruff format, mypy; 867 passed at 93.93% on Django 6.1.2;
867 passed with RLS_FAIL_ON_SKIPPED=1 on Django main (6.2.dev, asgiref
3.12.1) over the locked environment, the way the canary installs it.

commit.message:
ci: PostgreSQL 15/17 legs, zero-skipped rule, wheel smoke test, CHANGELOG gate (#110)

Close the four gaps between what the project claims and what CI proves.

PostgreSQL matrix: a new `test-postgres` job runs the suite on postgres:15 and
postgres:17 with the oldest and newest supported Django (4.2 on Python 3.12,
6.0 on Python 3.14). Four legs instead of widening the 15-leg matrix; 16 stays
the default everywhere else. README/docs now say CI runs 15, 16 and 17.

Zero-skipped rule: every PostgreSQL leg sets RLS_FAIL_ON_SKIPPED=1 and a
pytest_sessionfinish hook in tests/conftest.py (mirrored in the example suite)
fails the session when anything was skipped. Deselection and xfail do not
count. The one runtime pytest.skip() in the suite becomes a registered
`superuser_only` marker whose test fails with an explanatory message on a
plain role; deselect with -m "not superuser_only".

Wheel smoke: example-smoke now tests the built wheel, not the source tree.
`uv build`, an inline assertion that the wheel holds only django_rls_tenants/
and *.dist-info/ (every package dir has __init__.py; py.typed, the management
commands and contrib/celery.py are present; no bytecode), an install into a
clean .wheel-venv with the locked Django/test deps (uv export --group test
--no-emit-project), an isolated-mode import guard that the package resolves
inside the venv, then manage.py check, test collection,
makemigrations --check and the example suite as a non-superuser role.

CHANGELOG gate: publish.yml gains a `preflight` job that ci and docs depend
on. The release tag must be vX.Y.Z, equal pyproject.toml's version and have a
"## [X.Y.Z]" heading in CHANGELOG.md, otherwise nothing is built or published.
publish-testpypi.yml is untouched (it rewrites the version to .devN on purpose).

No library code changed. Verified locally against PostgreSQL 16: full suite
834 passed / 0 skipped with the rule on; the hook fails a probe skip and
ignores xfail/deselect; the wheel check passes; the example suite (36 tests)
passes against the wheel in a clean venv as the `app` role; the preflight
script passes for v1.3.2 and rejects v1.3.3 and a bare "1.3.2" tag.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HCnYnZA1K7yuFfg6CQ5dRj

fix(managers): keep LEFT JOIN for nested nullable select_related paths (#79)

TenantQuerySet.select_related("a__b") adds a tenant predicate on the
joined RLS-protected leaf table and, for nullable relations, ORs in
`a__b__isnull=True` so the join stays a LEFT OUTER JOIN. The nullability
check called `self.model._meta.get_field(field_path)` on the whole dotted
path, which raises FieldDoesNotExist (swallowed) for every multi-hop path.
No isnull clause was added, the predicate forced an INNER JOIN, and rows
whose chain had a NULL at any hop silently disappeared.

- New `_resolve_related_path()` walks the path segment by segment and
  returns `(target_model, nullable)`, where `nullable` is True when ANY
  hop is a nullable FK (or reverse one-to-one). `_resolve_related_model()`
  is now a thin wrapper over it.
- `select_related()` adds the `__isnull=True` escape hatch whenever the
  path is nullable; fully non-null chains keep their INNER JOIN, and
  single-hop behaviour is unchanged.
- Test models `OrderNoteAttachment` (nullable first hops) and
  `NoteRevision` (non-null first hops) + migration 0006 give all four
  shapes: nullable/nullable, nullable/non-null, non-null/nullable and
  non-null/non-null. Regression tests assert returned rows, SQL join
  types, the leaf tenant predicate and tenant isolation; the four
  row-preserving tests fail against the previous implementation.
- CHANGELOG and migration-guide (1.3.1 -> 1.3.2) entries.

Closes #79

Add M2M join table RLS support (#11)

Introduces subquery-based RLS policies for auto-generated M2M through
tables, ensuring tenant isolation extends to many-to-many relationships.

- RLSM2MConstraint: migration-aware constraint using EXISTS subqueries
- AddM2MRLSPolicy: reversible migration operation for M2M RLS policies
- register_m2m_rls(): auto-detection of M2M fields in AppConfig.ready()
- setup_m2m_rls: management command for retroactive RLS application
- check_rls: extended to verify M2M through table RLS coverage

Supports both-sides-protected, one-side-protected, and self-referential
M2M relationships. All SQL-interpolated inputs are validated against
injection via allowlists and regex checks.

Add strict mode for ORM-level tenant context enforcement (#14)

Introduce STRICT_MODE configuration that raises NoTenantContextError
when RLS-protected models are queried without an active tenant context,
providing defense-in-depth on top of database-level RLS policies.

Key changes:
- Add _rls_context_active ContextVar to track tenant context lifecycle
- Guard 12 queryset evaluation methods in TenantQuerySet
- Wire context tracking into tenant_context(), admin_context(), and middleware
- Add 29+ tests covering all guarded methods, context sources, and edge cases
- Update example app to demonstrate strict mode and error handling
- Comprehensive documentation across all guide and reference pages

Harden RLS security and improve auto-scoping feature

Security fixes:
- Add E001 system check detecting PostgreSQL superuser connections
  that silently bypass all RLS policies
- Guard against rls_tenant_id=None on non-admin users in
  _resolve_user_guc_vars (previously produced str(None) causing
  PostgreSQL cast errors)
- Migrate GUC-set flag from threading.local to ContextVar for
  proper isolation in ASGI/async deployments
- Fix W004 check to catch CONN_MAX_AGE=None (infinite connections)
- Skip unnecessary DB round-trips in cleanup for unauthenticated
  requests

Enhancements:
- Add select_related() tenant filter propagation to joined
  RLS-protected tables
- Export reset_current_tenant_id in public API
- Clarify CASE WHEN policy docs (clarity improvement, not perf)

Tests:
- Add concurrency tests verifying ContextVar thread isolation
- Add superuser check, None tenant_id, and select_related tests
- Add OrderItem model for cross-table join testing
Add ORM-level auto-scoping and optimize RLS policy structure

Address review findings: fix docs, harden safety nets, improve tests and performance

- Fix wrong setting keys in README quick-start (TENANT_FK_NAME -> TENANT_FK_FIELD, GUC_NAME -> GUC_PREFIX)
- Add unit tests for SQL-injection validation in GUC names, field names, PK types
- Gate request_finished safety net with threading.local flag to skip redundant cleanup
- Prevent vacuous pass in assert_rls_blocks_without_context on empty tables
- Add `using` parameter to all testing helpers for multi-database support
- Add is_local=True tests for rls_context, bypass_flag, tenant_context, admin_context
- Replace manual clear_guc cleanup with autouse fixture in conftest.py
- Add test for check_rls SystemExit(1) failure path
- Batch check_rls queries from 2N to 2 using IN clauses
- Eliminate N+1 in prepare_tenant_in_model_data by setting FK column directly
Add tests for tenants/ layer, integration, and layering enforcement
Add test infrastructure with models, fixtures, and migrations

Add project scaffolding with two-layer package structure, CI/CD, and docs

Set up django-rls-tenants with rls/ (generic RLS primitives) and tenants/
(Django multitenancy) layers, pytest/coverage/ruff/mypy tooling, GitHub
Actions CI matrix, and initial documentation.
